svg.title: Many simultaneous users on one scale — A noticeable difference in 1 of 6 tests
svg.desc: Many simultaneous users on one scale: A noticeable difference in 1 of 6 tests. Median per test for SQL Server, MySQL and PostgreSQL; all 6 tests share one axis from zero, so bar lengths compare across tests. Same scale for all 6 tests: 0 to 250 orders per minute: Enter sales orders – 4 clerks working non-stop, Enter sales orders – 8 clerks working non-stop, Enter sales orders – 16 clerks working non-stop, Everyone sells the best-seller – 4 clerks working non-stop, Everyone sells the best-seller – 8 clerks working non-stop and Everyone sells the best-seller – 16 clerks working non-stop. Coloured bars mark differences a user would notice, grey bars ties and differences too small to notice. Enter sales orders – 4 clerks working non-stop: Tie: no real winner. Enter sales orders – 8 clerks working non-stop: MySQL noticeably slower than PostgreSQL. Enter sales orders – 16 clerks working non-stop: Tie: no real winner. Everyone sells the best-seller – 4 clerks working non-stop: Tie: no real winner. Everyone sells the best-seller – 8 clerks working non-stop: Tie: no real winner. Everyone sells the best-seller – 16 clerks working non-stop: Tie: no real winner.

g.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, 'Liberation Sans', sans-serif

text.tspan: Many simultaneous users on one scale
A noticeable difference in 1 of 6 tests

g.text: Acumatica 2026 R2 · median of 6 runs per test and database · all 6 tests share one axis from zero, so bar lengths compare across tests

text.tspan: this database is on one side of a difference you would notice: noticeably faster or noticeably slower than another
no difference you would notice against the others. “tie” means inside the test’s noise margin; “not noticeable” means real

g.text: Same scale for all 6 tests: 0 to 250 orders per minute
All within 58%, inside the 75% noise margin. Gaps
are measured on the median time per order; the
per-minute medians differ more because SQL
orders per minute · higher is better
